addDesc: Once onboarded, the eight pages under Kubernetes start showing data. Read-only credentials are enough.
allReadyHint: Total node count — all of them ready. When some are not ready this shows as "ready/total" with the ready count highlighted.
deleteImpact: Collection stops immediately and the collected nodes, pods and workloads are removed with it (they are snapshots of this cluster and mean nothing without it). The cluster itself is untouched — we only read it.

discover.afterAdoptBody: GKE clusters connect through the service-account key of the cloud account they were discovered from, so no kubeconfig is needed. Go back to the cluster list, run “Test connection”, then “Sync now”. If the key lacks permissions (container.clusters.get plus read-only access inside the cluster), the connection test says so; you can also edit the cluster and paste a kubeconfig to override.
discover.desc: Use the cloud account's SA key to list every GKE cluster in that GCP project, then adopt the ones you want.
discover.noProjectHint: Discovery needs a cloud account SA key. Add an account and project under System → Cloud accounts first, and attach an SA key.
discover.none: No GKE clusters in this project.
discover.title: Discover GKE clusters

empty.filtered: No clusters match the current filters. Try widening them.
empty.noSource: No clusters yet. Use “Add” or “Discover from cloud account” at the top right of this page.
empty.title: No clusters

field.displayNameHint: A human-facing name such as “G32 Production”. Defaults to the cluster name.
field.kubeconfigHint: Read-only access (get/list/watch) is enough. Note the built-in view role excludes cluster-scoped resources such as nodes and fails with “nodes is forbidden” — do not reach for cluster-admin; a custom read-only ClusterRole is enough.
field.name: Cluster name
field.nameHint: Unique identifier; the kubectl context name is a good choice. Alerts and metrics usually carry it as the cluster label too.
field.promValueHint: The value of the cluster label in this cluster's Prometheus metrics. Required when it differs from the cluster name, otherwise every cluster-scoped query silently returns nothing.
field.providerHint: gke = Google Kubernetes Engine; anything else uses generic.

govern.capability: What can and cannot be determined on this cluster
govern.capacityNote: Limits above 100% mean overcommit — not necessarily wrong, but the first suspect when a node is under pressure.
govern.desc: Orphans, node capacity, failing pods, workload changes, security and config audit. All computed live, not from a snapshot.
govern.entryHint: Read-only drill-down across six views: orphaned resources, node capacity, namespace overview, workload changes, security audit, config audit. Nothing is modified
govern.noChanges: No workload changes in this window
govern.noConfigIssues: Config audit found nothing (mind the capability note above)
govern.platformHidden: {{count}} platform components hidden (CNI/CSI/monitoring — their privileges are by design). This list is not the full picture.
govern.unusedHint: Not checked by default — it scans every ConfigMap in the cluster. Being unreferenced is not a problem, just cleanup material.

sync.badCount: {{count}} of {{total}} resource types are not healthy. Data from those cannot support a conclusion.
sync.neverAny: This cluster has no collection records at all — nothing derived from it holds. That means collection never ran, not that the cluster is empty.
sync.title: Collection detail: when each resource type was last synced

title: Clusters
versionDriftHint: Nodes in this cluster run {{n}} different kubelet versions: {{list}}. A mix means an upgrade is in progress — or stuck, which will not resolve on its own
